name: Gabriel Christie
bio: a Representative from Maryland; born in Perryman, Harford County, Md., in 1755; served in the Revolutionary War,  member of a company of militia organized September 12, 1775, by the provincial convention held at Annapolis on July 26, 1775; member of the Maryland state house of delegates; appointed by Gov. William Smallwood one of the commissioners to "straighten and amend the post road from Havre de Grace to Baltimore town" by authority of the act of 1787; elected as an Anti-Administration candidate to the Third Congress, and reelected as a Democratic Republican to the Fourth Congress (March 4, 1793-March 3, 1797); elected as a Democratic Republican to the Sixth Congress (March 4, 1799-March 3, 1801); one of the commissioners of Havre de Grace in 1800 and 1801, and again in 1806; appointed collector of the port of Baltimore and served until his death; died on April 1, 1808, in Baltimore, Md.; interment at St. George's (Old Spesutia) Cemetery, Perryman, Harford County, Md.
